items.difficulty_reason: The helper lemma states that for a commutative square whose sheafified pushout and injectivity conditions hold, the canonical map attached to the square is an isomorphism for every complex in the essential image of the derived pushforward along epsilon (statement lines 6757-6776). The proof is short but complete: a K-injective representative is chosen so that its pushforward represents the given complex (proof lines 6782-6786), the blow-up square lemma supplies the short exact sequence of complexes attached to the square (proof lines 6787-6796), and the author observes that this is exactly the sequence defining the canonical map (proof lines 6797-6799). The non-formal content is the choice of representative and the identification of the two sequences. The claim is H1: a short reduction with two named inputs.
